newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU halts aid to Bosnian Serbs while Karadzic free.
newsitem.headline: EU halts aid to Bosnian Serbs while Karadzic free.

text.p: The European Commission ratcheted up pressure on indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic on Thursday, saying it was cutting off aid to the Bosnian Serbs until he was arrested.

In a statement, External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek said the arrest of Karadzic, the former Bosnian Serb president who still wields heavy behind-the-scenes power, was required by the Dayton peace agreement.
"The conditions of the Dayton agreement are very clear," he said. "War criminals must be handed to the War Crimes Tribunal if reconstruction aid is to be provided."
He also accused Karadzic of financial misconduct.
"Since most of the illegal economy is in his hands, we can no longer be sure that aid will not end up in his pockets," van den Broek's statement said.

The Republika Srpska, the Serb portion of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was due to receive 30 million European currency units ($34 million) from the Commission this year in aid to repair roads, telecommunications links and other reconstruction projects.

This was part of a total 200 million Ecus allocated by the Commission, the European Union's executive, for Bosnia as a whole. Last year, the Bosnian Serbs received 24 million Ecus out of 225 million Ecus for the divided country.
Van den Broek said that in line with international agreements the freeze on aid would not apply to humanitarian assistance for such things as orphanages and refugees.

Although the amount of money involved is relatively small, the move follows recent hints that the United States and its NATO allies are hardening their stance on the use of NATO troops in arresting war criminals.
NATO leaders, at a summit in Madrid this week, repeated calls for leaders in the region to fulfill their obligation to hand over all indicted war criminals to the international tribunal in The Hague.
But they held off any statement about changing NATO's role in the issue.
The Commission's move also comes as Bosnian Serb leader Biljana Plavsic has been battling for control with hardliners loyal to Karadzic.
Both the European Union and the United States have said Plavsic acted constitutionally when she dissolved the Bosnian Serb parliament last week.
